The proposed pipeline consists of three stages: preprocessing, detection and calorie estimation. During preprocessing, each input image is resized to 640 by 640 pixels and normalised using the channel-wise mean and standard deviation of the training set. Data augmentation is applied to improve generalisation, including random horizontal flips, colour jitter with a brightness factor of 0.2 and mosaic augmentation with a probability of 0.5. The detection stage employs a YOLOv8-small backbone pretrained on the COCO dataset, which is then fine-tuned for 100 epochs using stochastic gradient descent with an initial learning rate of 0.01 and a cosine annealing schedule. A batch size of 16 is used, and early stopping is triggered if the validation loss does not improve for 10 consecutive epochs. The final model achieves a mean average precision of 0.74 at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.5. In the calorie estimation stage, each detected bounding box is mapped to a food class, and the corresponding calorie value is retrieved from a lookup table derived from the Indian Food Composition Tables published by the National Institute of Nutrition.
